tagline: Up the Chilkat on an old trail, eagles in the cottonwoods.
intro: The old Tlingit name for Haines, Deishú, means end of the trail. The highway leaves town up the Chilkat River valley on a route Chilkat traders used long before it became the Dalton Trail and carried some of the Klondike prospectors. The Army built the road in 1943, in case the White Pass railroad out of Skagway was ever blocked. Year-round travel had to wait until 1963.

Only about 45 of its miles are in Alaska. From October into the new year hundreds of bald eagles roost in the cottonwoods beside the road, drawn by late runs of salmon. In June the river has fish wheels instead.

moments.title: Alaska Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve
moments.text: Miles 12 to 18 of the highway are the usual place to watch, and as many as 4,000 bald eagles have been counted here during the fall gathering.

moments.title: Klukwan
moments.text: Tlakw Aan means roughly the forever village, for its age, and it is the last of the five Chilkat villages that stood in the area before 1900.

moments.title: Porcupine
moments.text: Across the Klehini from mile 35, gold turned up on Porcupine Creek in 1898. When the district was listed in 1976, about 25 buildings still stood, in various stages of decay.
